items.articleText: EspressoLab'in BAE şirketine satışında yeni ayrıntı: İstenen fiyat belli oldu - Espressolab'in çoğunluk hissesinin yabancı bir şirkete devrine ilişkin yeni ayrıntılar ortaya çıktı. Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri merkezli MAIR Group'un finansal raporunda yer alan bilgiler, kahve zincirinin satış sürecine ilişkin daha önce açıklanmayan detayları gündeme taşıdı. MAIR Group P.J.S.C.’nin 11 Kasım’da yayımladığı ve KPMG incelemesinden geçen 30 Eylül 2026 tarihli özet konsolide ara dönem finansal tablolarında, Espressolab’ın çoğunluk hissesinin devrine ilişkin anlaşmanın mali ayrıntıları açıklandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Rapora göre MAIR Group, bir bağlı ortaklığı aracılığıyla ESLAB Kahve Gıda Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş.’nin çıkarılmış sermayesinin yüzde 70’ini satın almak üzere 23 Eylül 2026’da pay alım sözleşmesi (SPA) imzaladı. İşlemin tahmini satın alma bedeli, kapanış ön koşullarının yerine getirilmesine bağlı olarak yaklaşık 385 milyon Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri dirhemi (AED), diğer bir ifadeyle 105 milyon dolar olarak belirlendi. 58,7 milyon AED avans ödendi MAIR Group, 6 Mayıs 2026 tarihli ön mutabakat kapsamında satıcıya 58 milyon 727 bin AED tutarında avans ödemesi gerçekleştirdi. Ancak devir işlemi, yasal ve düzenleyici onayların beklenmesi nedeniyle 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla tamamlanmadı. Bu nedenle MAIR Group'un ara dönem finansal tablolarında söz konusu satın almaya ilişkin henüz bir işletme birleşmesi muhasebeleştirilmedi. Espressolab 21 ülkede 400'den fazla şubeye sahip MAIR Group'un finansal raporunda Espressolab'ın operasyonel büyüklüğüne ilişkin bilgilere de yer verildi. Ağustos 2026 itibarıyla 21 ülkede 400'den fazla kahve dükkanına sahip olan Espressolab'ın ağırlıklı olarak franchise iş modeliyle faaliyet gösterdiği belirtildi.

items.titleTr: Borsada yeni hedef 12.300 puan: Yükselişin önündeki son engel ne?
items.summaryTr: Borsa İstanbul'da sert satışların ardından yaşanan toparlanma yeni hedefleri gündeme taşıdı. CNBC-e'de konuşan Sertaç Ekeke, bu hafta 12.300 puanın görülebileceğini belirtirken, yükselişin devamı için yabancı yatırımcı girişine ve MSCI sürecine dikkat çekti.
items.articleText: Borsada yeni hedef 12.300 puan: Yükselişin önündeki son engel ne? Borsa İstanbul'da sert satışların ardından yaşanan toparlanma yeni hedefleri gündeme taşıdı. CNBC-e'de konuşan Sertaç Ekeke, bu hafta 12.300 puanın görülebileceğini belirtirken, yükselişin devamı için yabancı yatırımcı girişine ve MSCI sürecine dikkat çekti. Marbaş Menkul Değerler Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Sertaç Ekeke, CNBC-e ekranlarında yayınlanan Para Ekranı programında Şafak Tükle'nin sorularını yanıtladı. Borsa İstanbul'da sert satışların ardından önemli bir tepki yükselişi yaşandığını belirten Ekeke, endekste 12.000-12.300 puan seviyelerinin gündeme gelebileceğini söyledi. Ancak yükselişin kalıcı olabilmesi için yabancı yatırımcı girişinin kritik önem taşıdığına dikkat çekti. Borsa İstanbul'un yaklaşık 4 bin puanlık satışın ardından 10.600 puan seviyelerinden güçlü bir tepki verdiğini belirten Ekeke, yaklaşık 1.500 puanlık toparlanmaya rağmen piyasanın yükseliş momentumunda henüz istenilen seviyeye ulaşamadığını ifade etti. Bilanço döneminin tamamlandığını ve şirketlerin yüzde 25-30'luk bölümünde olumlu sayılabilecek finansal sonuçlar görüldüğünü dile getiren Ekeke, buna karşın piyasada tedirginliğin ve güven kaybının devam ettiğini söyledi. Ekeke, endekste bu haftaya ilişkin beklentisini şöyle açıkladı: "Ben bu hafta olası senaryoda 12.000-12.300 seviyelerinin görülebileceğini düşünüyorum. Ama aşağıda 11.500-11.300 hattını koruması lazım. Bu seviyelerin altında yeniden testere piyasasına döneriz." BIST 30 hisselerinde satış baskısı azaldı Borsadaki toparlanmanın önemli nedenlerinden birinin BIST 30 hisseleri üzerindeki satış baskısının azalması olduğunu belirten Ekeke, fonlardaki BIST 30 hisselerinin üç ay boyunca satılmamasına yönelik kararın piyasa açısından kritik olduğunu vurguladı. Söz konusu kararın yatırımcıların yeni bir satış dalgasıyla karşılaşma endişesini azalttığını ve piyasayı alıma yönelttiğini ifade eden Ekeke, buna rağmen henüz güçlü bir alım hareketinden söz etmek için erken olduğunu belirtti. Ekeke, iki yıldır hisse senedi taşıyan yatırımcıların zaten zorlu bir dönemden geçtiğini, fon kaynaklı satışların da bu mağduriyeti artırdığını söyledi. Alınan kararla BIST 30 üzerindeki baskının hafiflemesinin endekse olumlu yansıdığını kaydetti. MSCI kararları ay sonuna kadar baskı yaratabilir Borsa İstanbul'da yükselişin devamı için yabancı yatırımcının ikna edilmesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Ekeke, MSCI'ın Sabancı Holding (SAHOL) ve Astor Enerji'ye (ASTOR) ilişkin endeks değişikliklerine de değindi. Söz konusu değişiklikler nedeniyle ay sonuna kadar oluşabilecek satışların takip edilmesi gerektiğini belirten Ekeke, satışların derinleşmesini beklemediğini ancak bu sürecin piyasa üzerinde bir miktar baskı yaratabileceğini söyledi. "Genelde kötü haber dipte gelir" değerlendirmesinde bulunan Ekeke, yabancı yatırımcı oranının daha yüksek olması durumunda BIST 30 hisselerinde yaşanan sert satışların bu boyuta ulaşmayabileceğini ifade etti. Merkez Bankası'nın faiz mesajı kritik Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası'nın (TCMB) faiz indirim patikasında kalacağına yönelik verdiği mesajın piyasa açısından önemli olduğunu belirten Ekeke, enflasyon tahminlerinin yukarı yönlü revize edilmesinin ise şaşırtıcı olmadığını söyledi. Ekonomide harcama dinamiklerinin zayıfladığına ve ciddi bir soğuma yaşandığına dikkat çeken Ekeke, kredi kanallarının desteklenmesine yönelik adımların da bu çerçevede değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini ifade etti. Ekeke, harcamalardaki yavaşlamanın dezenflasyon sürecini desteklemesiyle Merkez Bankası'nın faiz indirimlerine devam edebileceğini belirtti. Mevcut faiz indirim patikasının borsa açısından şimdilik yeterli olduğunu söyleyen Ekeke, daha güçlü bir yükseliş için ise yabancı yatırımcı girişine ihtiyaç duyulduğunu vurguladı. "Momentum için bizim yabancıya ihtiyacımız var. Yerli yatırımcıda para yok. Yeni bir oyuncu girerse o zaman yeniden bakarız" dedi. Gözler Şimşek'in MSCI görüşmesinde Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek'in aralık ayında MSCI yetkilileriyle gerçekleştirmesi beklenen görüşmeyi de değerlendiren Ekeke, bu temasın Borsa İstanbul'un geleceği açısından önemli olabileceğini söyledi. MSCI'ın Türkiye'ye yönelik endişelerinin uzun süredir bilindiğini belirten Ekeke, kuruluşun artık somut adımlar görmek istediğini ifade etti. Endonezya örneğine de dikkat çeken Ekeke, MSCI ile ilişkilerin iyileştirilmesinin yabancı yatırımcıların Türkiye'ye bakışını olumlu etkileyebileceğini kaydetti. Ekeke, "MSCI'ın kaldırdığı bayrağın inmesi, 'oyuna devam' demesi önemli. MSCI'ın ikna edilmesi buranın asıl anahtarı. MSCI ile aramız düzelirse buradan daha iyi bir senaryo konuşabiliriz" ifadelerini kullandı.

"Genelde kötü haber dipte gelir" değerlendirmesinde bulunan Ekeke, yabancı yatırımcı oranının daha yüksek olması durumunda BIST 30 hisselerinde yaşanan sert satışların bu boyuta ulaşmayabileceğini ifade etti. Merkez Bankası'nın faiz mesajı kritik Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası'nın (TCMB) faiz indirim patikasında kalacağına yönelik verdiği mesajın piyasa açısından önemli olduğunu belirten Ekeke, enflasyon tahminlerinin yukarı yönlü revize edilmesinin ise şaşırtıcı olmadığını söyledi. Ekonomide harcama dinamiklerinin zayıfladığına ve ciddi bir soğuma yaşandığına dikkat çeken Ekeke, kredi kanallarının desteklenmesine yönelik adımların da bu çerçevede değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini ifade etti. Ekeke, harcamalardaki yavaşlamanın dezenflasyon sürecini desteklemesiyle Merkez Bankası'nın faiz indirimlerine devam edebileceğini belirtti. Mevcut faiz indirim patikasının borsa açısından şimdilik yeterli olduğunu söyleyen Ekeke, daha güçlü bir yükseliş için ise yabancı yatırımcı girişine ihtiyaç duyulduğunu vurguladı. "Momentum için bizim yabancıya ihtiyacımız var. Yerli yatırımcıda para yok. Yeni bir oyuncu girerse o zaman yeniden bakarız" dedi. Gözler Şimşek'in MSCI görüşmesinde Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek'in aralık ayında MSCI yetkilileriyle gerçekleştirmesi beklenen görüşmeyi de değerlendiren Ekeke, bu temasın Borsa İstanbul'un geleceği açısından önemli olabileceğini söyledi. MSCI'ın Türkiye'ye yönelik endişelerinin uzun süredir bilindiğini belirten Ekeke, kuruluşun artık somut adımlar görmek istediğini ifade etti. Endonezya örneğine de dikkat çeken Ekeke, MSCI ile ilişkilerin iyileştirilmesinin yabancı yatırımcıların Türkiye'ye bakışını olumlu etkileyebileceğini kaydetti. Ekeke, "MSCI'ın kaldırdığı bayrağın inmesi, 'oyuna devam' demesi önemli. MSCI'ın ikna edilmesi buranın asıl anahtarı. MSCI ile aramız düzelirse buradan daha iyi bir senaryo konuşabiliriz" ifadelerini kullandı.

items.summary: ABD Gıda ve İlaç Dairesi (FDA), AstraZeneca'nın mesane kanseri tedavisinde kullanılan Imfinzi ilacının yeni kullanımına ve nadir kas güçsüzlüğü hastalığına yönelik Klygefa tedavisine onay verdi.

items.titleTr: İlaç devi, yeni nadir hastalık tedavisi için ABD'den onay aldı
items.summaryTr: ABD Gıda ve İlaç Dairesi (FDA), AstraZeneca'nın mesane kanseri tedavisinde kullanılan Imfinzi ilacının yeni kullanımına ve nadir kas güçsüzlüğü hastalığına yönelik Klygefa tedavisine onay verdi.
items.articleText: İlaç devi, yeni nadir hastalık tedavisi için ABD'den onay aldı - ABD Gıda ve İlaç Dairesi (FDA), AstraZeneca'nın mesane kanseri tedavisinde kullanılan Imfinzi ilacının yeni kullanımına ve nadir kas güçsüzlüğü hastalığına yönelik Klygefa tedavisine onay verdi. İngiliz ilaç şirketi AstraZeneca, ABD Gıda ve İlaç Dairesinden (FDA) iki ilaç onayı aldı. Şirketin immünoterapi ilacı Imfinzi'nin mesane kanserinde kullanım alanı genişletilirken, nadir görülen kas güçsüzlüğü hastalığına yönelik Klygefa adlı tedavinin de kullanımına izin verildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Reuters'ın haberine göre FDA, Imfinzi'nin enfortumab vedotin adlı hedefe yönelik tedaviyle birlikte, kas dokusuna ilerlemiş mesane kanseri hastalarında ameliyat öncesinde kullanılmasını onayladı. Onay, sisplatin bazlı kemoterapi alamayan veya bu tedaviyi kabul etmeyen hastaları kapsıyor. İleri aşama klinik araştırmanın sonuçlarına dayanan onay kapsamında, söz konusu tedavi kombinasyonunun kanserin nüksetme riskini yüzde 49, ölüm riskini ise yüzde 42 azalttığı belirtildi. Imfinzi, halihazırda 50'den fazla ülkede onaylı bulunuyor ve akciğer ile mesane kanserinin de aralarında bulunduğu çeşitli kanser türlerinde kullanılıyor. Nadir hastalığa yönelik tedaviye de onay FDA, AstraZeneca'nın nadir hastalıklar birimi Alexion tarafından geliştirilen Klygefa adlı ilaca da onay verdi. İlaç, sinirler ile kaslar arasındaki iletişimi bozarak kas güçsüzlüğüne yol açan genelleşmiş miyastenia gravis (gMG) hastalığı bulunan ve sinirlerdeki proteinleri hedef alan antikorları taşıyan yetişkin hastalarda kullanılacak. Klygefa, aynı gün Avrupa Birliği'nde de aynı hastalık için onay aldı. İlaç, belirli gMG hastalarında kullanılmak üzere Japonya ve bazı diğer ülkelerde de ruhsatlandırılmıştı.

items.titleTr: US basketball player arrested with 34kg of cannabis at Nigerian airport
items.summaryTr: The anti-drugs agency says the American attempted to leave the airport, abandoning his luggage with the drugs.
items.articleText: US basketball player arrested with 34kg of cannabis at Nigerian airport - Published A basketball player from the US has been arrested in Nigeria with 33.95kg (75lbs) of cannabis in his luggage at the main airport in Lagos. The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) identified the player as Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, from the US state of Georgia, who it said had arrived from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates. According to the agency, the suspect said he had been playing professional basketball in Thailand and was visiting to Nigeria to "build networks" for his career. He has not publicly commented on the allegations. The agency said an examination of the suspect's phone had pointed "to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity". In statement on Sunday, the agency he was arrested on Wednesday after airport officials noticed him abandoning his two checked-in bags and attempting to leave with his carry-on bag. The two bags, which bore his name, contained 32 packs of the drug known as "Loud", a potent strain of cannabis, the agency said. A tracking device was also recovered from the bags, the agency added. The International Basketball Federation (FIBA) lists a player by the name Damonte Greene, with the most recent appearance at the Phuket Elite Cup in Thailand, on 26 September. Nigeria, once regarded primarily as a transit hub for drug trafficking, has increasingly become a producer, consumer, and distributor of illegal drugs, according to the UN. Recent NDLEA operations have uncovered several industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories, raising concerns about links between Nigerian drug producers and Mexican cartels seeking to manufacture and export the drug. In September, the agency said it had dismantled a meth lab and arrested a Mexican suspected drug kingpin who was allegedly attempting to flee Nigeria through Lagos. Methamphetamine, commonly known as meth, is a highly addictive synthetic drug that can cause severe psychosis, heart attacks or stroke. In August, a social media influencer suspected of links to an international drug trafficking network was arrested after the authorities seized cocaine worth nearly $28m (£21m), which was destined for the UK. items.summary: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Yemeni forces' retreat leaves Houthis in control of key area on coast of Red Sea waterway
items.summaryTr: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden.
items.articleText: Yemeni forces' retreat leaves Houthis in control of key area on coast of Red Sea waterway - Published Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia have said they are withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, leaving it under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement. Yemen's military said it was redeploying troops from the key shipping gateway at the southern end of the Red Sea to defend its interim capital, Aden. The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the waterway after the Houthis seized it in a surprise offensive in September, squeezing global oil exports and prompting thousands to flee. Houthi-run media reported later on Sunday the group had taken control of the territory. Saudi Arabia has not commented. Pro-government forces said they had "secured" the strait in early October as they sought to retake crucial ground from the Houthis, who said they had captured areas including Perim Island at the mouth of the strait and the strategic port city of Mokha a month prior. But the Saudi-backed forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Sunday they were withdrawing to reinforce troops elsewhere, with the southern city of Aden a "priority". The Southern Armed Forces' statement said troops were being withdrawn "from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area". It said the decision had been made with the aim of "strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats". "This step is driven by the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and neighbouring governorates, reinforcing the front lines and addressing existing threats." The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway when they captured it, but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia. However, the seizure contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. A UN Human Rights spokesperson, Ravina Shamdasani, urged all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure. She noted that since the escalation of fighting in August, more than 60% of documented civilian casualties were women and children. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked the city of Aden in recent weeks, including an assault on 15 October that targeted the presidential palace, killing five and injuring 16. Saudi Arabia responded with hundreds of air strikes, while the Houthis launched hundreds of drones and missiles at its cities and infrastructure. The UN has estimated that nearly 330,000 people have been displaced in Yemen as the fighting has since escalated. Hundreds of people are reported to have been killed. - Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway - Published6 October - Yemenis flee across Red Sea as Houthis and Saudi-backed forces escalate war - Published21 September Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from its capital, Sanaa. items.articleTextTr: Yemeni forces' retreat leaves Houthis in control of key area on coast of Red Sea waterway - Published Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia have said they are withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, leaving it under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement. Yemen's military said it was redeploying troops from the key shipping gateway at the southern end of the Red Sea to defend its interim capital, Aden. The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the waterway after the Houthis seized it in a surprise offensive in September, squeezing global oil exports and prompting thousands to flee. Houthi-run media reported later on Sunday the group had taken control of the territory. Saudi Arabia has not commented. Pro-government forces said they had "secured" the strait in early October as they sought to retake crucial ground from the Houthis, who said they had captured areas including Perim Island at the mouth of the strait and the strategic port city of Mokha a month prior. But the Saudi-backed forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Sunday they were withdrawing to reinforce troops elsewhere, with the southern city of Aden a "priority". The Southern Armed Forces' statement said troops were being withdrawn "from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area". It said the decision had been made with the aim of "strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats". "This step is driven by the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and neighbouring governorates, reinforcing the front lines and addressing existing threats." The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway when they captured it, but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia. However, the seizure contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. A UN Human Rights spokesperson, Ravina Shamdasani, urged all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure. She noted that since the escalation of fighting in August, more than 60% of documented civilian casualties were women and children. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked the city of Aden in recent weeks, including an assault on 15 October that targeted the presidential palace, killing five and injuring 16. Saudi Arabia responded with hundreds of air strikes, while the Houthis launched hundreds of drones and missiles at its cities and infrastructure. items.titleTr: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light
items.summaryTr: Ministers last month announced the Jackdaw gas field, which lies 150 miles east of Aberdeen, had been approved after years of uncertainty.
items.articleText: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light - Published Gas has begun flowing from the Jackdaw gas field, with the UK energy secretary saying it will help to heat millions of homes and businesses this winter. Ministers last month announced the Jackdaw field, which lies 150 miles east of Aberdeen, had been approved after years of uncertainty and a court case. It has now been announced that it has begun producing gas which will start flowing into Britain, according to its operator Adura. The UK government approved production from the gas field in the North Sea last month, amid intense debate about the project's environmental and economic impact. Jackdaw is operated by Adura under a joint venture between Shell and Norwegian state energy firm Equinor. A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, which is located off the coast of Shetland in the North Atlantic. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said: "Last month, I gave Jackdaw the green light and today its gas will start flowing into Britain, thanks to the hard work of the skilled North Sea workers. "It means homegrown gas from this project will help to heat millions of British homes and businesses this winter and beyond, in a boost for our energy security. "It also will help minimise the UK's use of imported higher emission gas as we continue our transition to renewables and nuclear." Claire Mueller, Jackdaw project director at Adura, said the gas field was "now helping to power Britain". She added: "At a time of considerable uncertainty around the world, Jackdaw will provide secure energy from our own waters to heat British homes and power our economy, while reducing our reliance on imports with higher emissions. "Jackdaw also demonstrates what can be achieved when Britain makes pragmatic, evidence-led decisions about the energy it needs, while properly accounting for our climate responsibilities." Mueller said the decision was a "positive step towards restoring confidence in the North Sea". She added that Adura was "proud to be producing the oil and gas our country will continue to need for decades". Adura has said Jackdaw will provide about 6% of UK gas production, enough to power 1.4 million homes. After imports are included, that amounts to about 2% of total UK demand. The gas will be pumped to the existing Shearwater platform for processing – known as a tie-back in industry terms – before being piped to the St Fergus gas terminal in Aberdeenshire. The UK government said that over its expected 11-year lifespan, Jackdaw would support the UK's gas supply, protect hundreds of jobs and add £2.9bn to the economy. The timeline of Jackdaw and Rosebank The decision to green-light Jackdaw drew criticism from some Labour backbenchers and environmentalists, while Conservatives called on the government to also approve the Rosebank oil field. Both projects were approved for development by the previous Tory government in 2022 and 2023 respectively but these decisions were struck down by the Scottish courts after a challenge from environmental campaigners. This followed a Supreme Court ruling that developers had to account for the climate impact caused by burning fossil fuels in their planning applications. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to stick to the UK's net zero target despite giving the green light to Jackdaw. He previously said the decision would "significantly strengthen our energy security by increasing domestic gas production by about 6% and support the UK's energy supply for more than a decade". A decision on the larger Rosebank oil project is yet to be made. The co-leader of the Scottish Greens, Ross Greer, described the Jackdaw approval as "climate vandalism". He said: "It is a devastating betrayal of our children's future and it won't even lower energy bills in the here and now." Environmental campaigners argue that this summer's heatwaves demonstrate the need to tackle climate change by rejecting both Jackdaw and Rosebank. Areeba Hamid, the co-executive director of Greenpeace, said approving Jackdaw was "the wrong decision" in terms of lowering energy bills, providing energy security, and addressing climate change. Oxfam said the government had "drilled straight through the UK's climate commitments" and accused the prime minister of sending "the wrong signal as the impacts of climate change intensify". The charity says the government must commit to not approving any new oil and gas licences, including the proposals for Rosebank. Jackdaw sits close to the boundary between the British and Norwegian sectors of the North Sea, in an area where Westminster originally granted licences to explore for oil and gas in 1970 and 1989. The field was discovered in 2005 but it was expensive and technically difficult to exploit. Shell did not commit to its development until 2022, shortly after the Conservative government had granted consent for production. But in January 2025, after a challenge by environmentalists, the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled that consent for Jackdaw and Rosebank had been granted unlawfully. The judge, Lord Ericht, said the developers should have provided a more detailed account of the fields' impact on climate change as part of the permitting process. The judge allowed the companies to continue with preparatory work short of producing oil and gas while they crafted new environmental impact assessments taking into account the eventual effect of actually burning the fossil fuels, not just the emissions which would be created in extracting them. On the Front Line: Inside the Platform An inside look at Jackdaw, the UK’s newest and most contested gas platform. When BBC News visited the platform this summer, Adura CEO Neil McCulloch said its approval was vital to avoid domestic supply shortages this winter. However, the UK government has previously suggested that Jackdaw will have little impact on energy security and none on reducing domestic gas and electricity bills. In August, in an interim response to a consultation on the future of the country's gas supplies, Energy Minister Michael Shanks said the UK would inevitably become more reliant on imports as domestic production declined, external. "With diminishing output from the North Sea over the past decades, any gas produced from the UK Continental Shelf represents a tiny fraction of global demand and so will not lower prices nor materially boost supply," wrote Shanks. Labour has previously said it is opposed to the issuing of new exploration licences but it will consider new production projects if they are tied back to existing facilities. McCulloch described the Jackdaw decision as "an important and positive step forward" - but said attention now turned to Rosebank. He has urged the UK government to approve production from the field, in which Adura owns an 80% stake. The other 20% is held by London-based Ithaca Energy. Rosebank contains an estimated 300 million to 500 million barrels of oil. But while most of Jackdaw's gas is likely to be consumed in the UK, Rosebank's oil will be taken off by tanker and sold on international markets. This followed a Supreme Court ruling that developers had to account for the climate impact caused by burning fossil fuels in their planning applications. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to stick to the UK's net zero target despite giving the green light to Jackdaw. He previously said the decision would "significantly strengthen our energy security by increasing domestic gas production by about 6% and support the UK's energy supply for more than a decade". A decision on the larger Rosebank oil project is yet to be made. The co-leader of the Scottish Greens, Ross Greer, described the Jackdaw approval as "climate vandalism". He said: "It is a devastating betrayal of our children's future and it won't even lower energy bills in the here and now." Environmental campaigners argue that this summer's heatwaves demonstrate the need to tackle climate change by rejecting both Jackdaw and Rosebank. Areeba Hamid, the co-executive director of Greenpeace, said approving Jackdaw was "the wrong decision" in terms of lowering energy bills, providing energy security, and addressing climate change. Oxfam said the government had "drilled straight through the UK's climate commitments" and accused the prime minister of sending "the wrong signal as the impacts of climate change intensify". The charity says the government must commit to not approving any new oil and gas licences, including the proposals for Rosebank. Jackdaw sits close to the boundary between the British and Norwegian sectors of the North Sea, in an area where Westminster originally granted licences to explore for oil and gas in 1970 and 1989. The field was discovered in 2005 but it was expensive and technically difficult to exploit. Shell did not commit to its development until 2022, shortly after the Conservative government had granted consent for production. But in January 2025, after a challenge by environmentalists, the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled that consent for Jackdaw and Rosebank had been granted unlawfully. The judge, Lord Ericht, said the developers should have provided a more detailed account of the fields' impact on climate change as part of the permitting process. The judge allowed the companies to continue with preparatory work short of producing oil and gas while they crafted new environmental impact assessments taking into account the eventual effect of actually burning the fossil fuels, not just the emissions which would be created in extracting them. On the Front Line: Inside the Platform An inside look at Jackdaw, the UK’s newest and most contested gas platform. When BBC News visited the platform this summer, Adura CEO Neil McCulloch said its approval was vital to avoid domestic supply shortages this winter. However, the UK government has previously suggested that Jackdaw will have little impact on energy security and none on reducing domestic gas and electricity bills. In August, in an interim response to a consultation on the future of the country's gas supplies, Energy Minister Michael Shanks said the UK would inevitably become more reliant on imports as domestic production declined, external. "With diminishing output from the North Sea over the past decades, any gas produced from the UK Continental Shelf represents a tiny fraction of global demand and so will not lower prices nor materially boost supply," wrote Shanks. Labour has previously said it is opposed to the issuing of new exploration licences but it will consider new production projects if they are tied back to existing facilities. McCulloch described the Jackdaw decision as "an important and positive step forward" - but said attention now turned to Rosebank. He has urged the UK government to approve production from the field, in which Adura owns an 80% stake. The other 20% is held by London-based Ithaca Energy. Rosebank contains an estimated 300 million to 500 million barrels of oil. But while most of Jackdaw's gas is likely to be consumed in the UK, Rosebank's oil will be taken off by tanker and sold on international markets. items.titleTr: 'Break-in and rising costs could kill my business'
items.summaryTr: Gordon Kidd says if things do not improve financially, he fears his firm in Shifnal will go under.
items.articleText: 'Break-in and rising costs could kill my business' - Published The owner of a cycle shop says he is considering closing the business after a break-in and soaring costs. Gordon Kidd, who runs Shifnal Cycles, estimates that a burglary last month cost him about £20,000 after three customer bikes and a frame were stolen and the subsequent repairs to his shop. Along with rising bills and a "lack of government support", the former armed forces veteran said the business in Shifnal may not be viable if financial pressures continue. A government spokesperson said that, from next year, businesses such as cycle shops would see their business rates either frozen, reduced or cut to zero, with half of the high-street retailers paying no rates. West Mercia Police said it had received a report of a burglary on 31 October, and an investigation was ongoing. "They stole customers' bikes, which, for me, as a shop owner, is my biggest fear," said Kidd, who was concerned the burglary could affect his reputation. "That might put them [customers] off from using my shop, and that kills a shop." He added: "I've got to do what's financially viable for the business. "I've got to look at another avenue now, and I've got to look at a more cost-effective way of doing it." Alongside coping with the impact of the burglary, Kidd called on the government to do more to help small businesses. "I don't know how the government expects small businesses to operate and make a living," he said. "We just break even with the repairs side of things, and it's tough." He said the break-in "had not helped whatsoever". "A lot of people probably think that bike shops make a lot of money when we really don't," he said. 'My cycle shop is like therapy' Kidd, who not only sells cycles but also repairs and services them, told the BBC that the break-in had made him feel angry that his safe space had been invaded. He suffers post-traumatic stress disorder and said the business was "like therapy". "Working on bikes calms me down; it helps me keep in control of my PTSD and my mental health in general." A government spokesperson said: "Corporation tax remains capped, and there are generous tax reliefs offered for hiring young people. "We are also making the business environment work better through our £4.3bn business rates support package, small business plan and action on late payments. items.titleTr: Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election
items.summaryTr: There has not been an election in Haiti since before the death of Jovenel Moise in 2021.
items.articleText: Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election - Published The widow of assassinated former Haitian president Jovenel Moise has registered as a presidential candidate for next year's elections in the Caribbean nation. Martine Moise was injured in the gun attack that killed her husband at their home in the capital, Port-au-Prince, in 2021. Haiti, which last held an election in 2016, has been plagued with chronic instability and gang violence. Elections were scheduled to be held in December but were postponed last month until July due to the country's insecurity. Moise has to comment on her candidacy but the electoral council website showed her registration on Sunday. Last week she said on X: "Haiti will rise again on its own two feet, because politics needs to be done differently." A total of 33 candidates have registered for the elections, including former presidents Michel Martelly and Jocelerme Privert, former prime minister Claude Joseph and former foreign minister Dominique Dupuy. Jovenel Moise, who led Haiti from 2017 until his death, was shot dead at his home in Port-au-Prince in July 2021, allegedly by a group of mainly Colombian mercenaries. Martine Moise suffered serious gunshot wounds during the attack and was flown to a hospital in Florida. She was charged in connection with the assassination in 2024, but the indictment was overturned last year. The assassination shook the Caribbean nation to its core, with many Haitians shocked that the 53-year-old was killed with such apparent ease. Thirty suspects have been indicted over the killing so far and in September 18 people were flown from Haiti to Florida to stand trial for their alleged involvement in the assassination. Haiti has been engulfed in a wave of gang violence since the assassination of Moise. At least 1,408 people were killed and 656 injured from April through to June this year, according to the UN Integrated Office in Haiti.
